indicator.name: CoinMarketCap Crypto Market Metrics
indicator.description: A market-wide daily snapshot from CoinMarketCap containing aggregate cryptocurrency market capitalization, trading volume, market-share measures, sector-level market capitalization and volume, derivatives activity, market growth rates, and ecosystem activity statistics. The dataset provides a broad view of crypto-market size, liquidity, market structure, capital distribution, and changes in market activity within a single observation.
indicator.use: Monitor the overall size, liquidity, composition, activity, and structural changes of the cryptocurrency market using CoinMarketCap's aggregate market metrics.
indicator.purpose: Provide a consolidated market-wide snapshot for understanding total crypto-market capitalization, trading activity, Bitcoin and Ethereum market share, altcoin and DeFi market size, stablecoin liquidity, derivatives activity, and changes in the broader crypto ecosystem.
indicator.significance: CoinMarketCap Crypto Market Metrics provides broad market context that can be used to interpret changes across individual crypto assets and specialized indicators. Total market capitalization measures the aggregate value of the cryptocurrency market, while 24-hour spot trading volume provides a measure of market activity and liquidity. Altcoin market capitalization and volume help isolate activity outside Bitcoin, while Bitcoin and Ethereum dominance measure their respective shares of the total cryptocurrency market and can provide context for capital distribution and rotation. DeFi market capitalization and volume provide visibility into decentralized-finance activity, while stablecoin market capitalization and volume provide context for the size and activity of crypto-native liquidity instruments. Derivatives volume provides a measure of activity in crypto derivatives markets. The dataset also includes daily percentage changes in total market capitalization, total volume, DeFi activity, stablecoin activity, and derivatives activity, allowing the system to identify rapid changes in market conditions. Active cryptocurrency, market-pair, and exchange counts provide additional context for the size and breadth of the crypto ecosystem. These metrics can be analyzed alongside asset prices, market breadth, volatility, derivatives positioning, funding rates, stablecoin indicators, Bitcoin dominance, DeFi indicators, and macroeconomic conditions to identify changes in liquidity, market participation, capital rotation, and broader crypto-market regimes.

indicator.name: Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index
indicator.description: A daily composite index from Alternative.me measuring crypto-market sentiment on a scale from 0 to 100, where lower values represent greater fear and higher values represent greater greed. Alternative.me derives the index from multiple sentiment-related inputs, including Bitcoin volatility, market momentum and volume, social media activity, surveys, Bitcoin dominance, and Google Trends. Alternative.me's published methodology currently identifies the index as Bitcoin-focused.
indicator.use: Track daily changes in aggregate crypto-market sentiment using Alternative.me's composite Fear & Greed Index and its fear-to-greed classification.
indicator.purpose: Provide a standardized daily measure of market sentiment that can be used to identify shifts between fear, neutrality, and greed in the crypto market.
indicator.significance: The Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index combines multiple market and sentiment signals into a single 0-to-100 measure. Alternative.me's published methodology assigns 25% weight to volatility, 25% to market momentum and volume, 15% to social media, 15% to surveys, 10% to Bitcoin dominance, and 10% to Google Trends, although Alternative.me currently states that its surveys are paused. The index therefore captures several dimensions of market behavior rather than directly measuring investor sentiment through a single survey. It can be analyzed alongside price trends, volatility, trading volume, derivatives positioning, funding rates, market breadth, Bitcoin dominance, and other sentiment indicators to provide broader context for changes in crypto-market conditions.

indicator.name: CoinMarketCap Altcoin Season Index
indicator.description: A daily CoinMarketCap index measuring the relative performance of major altcoins versus Bitcoin over a rolling 90-day period. The index uses the top 100 eligible coins ranked on CoinMarketCap, excluding stablecoins and wrapped or asset-backed tokens, and scales the proportion of coins outperforming Bitcoin to a 0-to-100 index.
indicator.use: Track the degree to which major altcoins are outperforming or underperforming Bitcoin over a rolling 90-day period and identify shifts between Bitcoin-dominant and altcoin-dominant market regimes.
indicator.purpose: Provide a standardized measure of altcoin market breadth relative to Bitcoin and identify broad changes in relative performance across the cryptocurrency market.
indicator.significance: The CoinMarketCap Altcoin Season Index measures market breadth by comparing the rolling 90-day performance of the top 100 eligible coins on CoinMarketCap against Bitcoin. Stablecoins and wrapped or asset-backed tokens are excluded from the constituent set. The index reflects the proportion of these coins outperforming Bitcoin and is scaled from 1 to 100. Values above 75 indicate Altcoin Season, while values at or below 25 indicate Bitcoin Season. The index therefore measures the breadth of altcoin outperformance rather than sentiment directly: a high value means a large share of major altcoins have outperformed Bitcoin over the measurement period, while a low value means relatively few have done so. It can be analyzed alongside Bitcoin dominance, altcoin market capitalization, market breadth, liquidity, trading volume, and crypto-market sentiment to provide context for changes in market regime and capital rotation.

indicator.name: Bitcoin Spot ETF Market
indicator.description: A daily measure of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF market activity, including aggregate net capital flows, traded value, net assets, and cumulative net flows. The indicator provides a view of capital entering or leaving the Bitcoin spot ETF market and the size and activity of the investment vehicles providing regulated market access to Bitcoin.
indicator.use: Track daily capital flows, trading activity, assets under management, and cumulative capital flows in the U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF market.
indicator.purpose: Provide a daily view of institutional and traditional-finance market participation in Bitcoin through regulated spot ETF vehicles and identify changes in capital allocation toward Bitcoin.
indicator.significance: Bitcoin spot ETF market data provides a direct view of capital flows and asset levels within regulated investment vehicles that give traditional investors access to Bitcoin. Net flow measures the daily net movement of capital into or out of the ETF market, while value traded measures ETF trading activity. Net assets indicate the aggregate size of assets held through the ETF vehicles, and cumulative net flow tracks the longer-term accumulation of capital flows since the measurement period began. Bitcoin ETF activity can provide important context for institutional and traditional-finance participation in Bitcoin and can be analyzed alongside Bitcoin price, Bitcoin dominance, derivatives positioning, open interest, funding rates, macroeconomic conditions, inflation expectations, interest rates, Treasury yields, liquidity conditions, and broader crypto-market sentiment. ETF flows should be interpreted as activity within the spot Bitcoin ETF market and should not be treated as a complete measure of all institutional Bitcoin ownership or total Bitcoin demand.

indicator.use: Track changes in Bitcoin futures open interest and positioning across dealers, asset managers, leveraged funds, other reportable traders, and nonreportable traders, including shifts in long, short, spreading, and net exposure.
indicator.purpose: Provide asset-specific visibility into how different classes of market participants are positioned in Bitcoin futures and how their exposure changes over time.

Changes in open interest reveal changes in futures-market participation, while changes in long and short positions show how each trader group is adjusting directional exposure. Separating trader classifications allows the intelligence system to distinguish institutional and leveraged positioning from dealer activity and aggregate nonreportable participation when analyzing Bitcoin market structure and sentiment.

items.headline: The Bitcoin ups and downs continue but with the sellers taking back short term control
items.summary: Bitcoin spent the last few days trying to break through the upper swing area between $85,578 and $87,374, but buyers could not get the price above the ceiling. Friday’s high reached $87,144, just short of the upper extreme. Monday’s high was a little lower at $86,969, and yesterday’s high stalled at $86,677 before rotating to the downside. Those progressively lower highs suggested the upside push was losing momentum. Buyers had their shot. They could not finish the job. The moving average breaks gave sellers the shove Despite the failed attempts near the highs, buyers continued to lean against the rising 100-hour moving average — the blue line on the chart below — and the rising 200-hour moving average, shown in green. Those levels helped keep the recovery alive. That changed today. The price broke below both moving averages, shifting the short-term bias in favor of the sellers. With support giving way, downside momentum accelerated and took bitcoin to $82,734. That low was just inside the upper boundary of the next swing area between $81,517 and $82,833. See the hourly chart below. Sellers have control, but another hurdle remains The moving average breaks were a win for sellers. However, extending that control requires more work. The $81,517–$82,833 swing area is the next key test. Trading near its upper boundary puts the area in play, but sellers still need to push through the zone and get below $81,517 — and stay below it. That would strengthen the bearish bias and open the door for further downside momentum. Conversely, if buyers can hold support within the area and move back above $82,833, they would have a foothold for a recovery. The broken moving averages would then become the upside targets and resistance: 200-hour moving average: $84,799 100-hour moving average: $85,269 Moving above the 200-hour MA would begin to repair the technical damage. Getting above both moving averages and staying above them would shift the short-term bias back toward the buyers. Until then, sellers retain the advantage. Trader education: Support defines risk, but buyers need follow-through For newer traders, the lesson is that failed attempts at resistance become more meaningful when support finally breaks. The lower highs were a warning. Today’s move below the moving averages supplied the shove. The lower swing area now gives buyers a place to lean and define their risk. However, holding support is only the first step. Buyers also need to reclaim broken levels to show they are taking back control. Hold the swing area and buyers have a chance to regroup. Break below $81,517 and stay below, and sellers strengthen their grip. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

highlights: Tether Signs MoU with the National Bank of Kazakhstan and the Alatau City Authority to Explore Stablecoin Use Cases and Asset Tokenization - Tether.io 7 October 2026 – Tether, the largest company in the digital asset industry, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the National Bank of Kazakhstan (NBK) and the Alatau City Authority (ACA), a specialized state administrative body in Kazakhstan. Together, the parties will explore opportunities in stablecoin development, asset tokenization, and decentralized finance. The NBK is the central bank of the Republic of Kazakhstan. It is responsible for developing and implementing monetary policy, overseeing payment systems, managing currency regulation and control, and maintaining the stability of the country’s financial system. The ACA is responsible for public administration and regulatory development in the city of Alatau under its special legal regime. It was established to position the city as a hub for digital innovation and financial technology in Central Asia. Under the MoU, the parties will work to develop the infrastructure needed to support digital finance in Kazakhstan. This includes jointly studying international models for stablecoin issuance, defining potential use cases, and preparing a concept and pilot proposal for a stablecoin pegged to the national currency, the tenge. The agreement also covers developing an asset tokenization framework in Kazakhstan, including the potential use of Hadron by Tether, Tether’s tokenization platform. Drawing on international regulatory and technological experience, the parties will identify priority asset categories, design a conceptual tokenization model, and launch a pilot project within the jurisdiction of the city of Alatau. To support these efforts, Tether, the NBK, and the ACA will hold a series of educational workshops, seminars, and training programs. These will cover the international stablecoin and digital asset market, issuance and reserve management models, and the tokenization of real-world assets using distributed ledger technology, while supporting the professional development of NBK specialists and relevant government agencies. “The use cases for digital assets are evolving into real-life applications and, ultimately, into sovereign level financial infrastructure. Kazakhstan is taking a deliberate, forward-looking approach by exploring asset tokenization and a strategic reserve framework. We are proud to support this vision for financial innovation and technological advancement across Central Asia. Our goal is to build efficient, transparent, and sustainable digital finance infrastructure, while protecting data and privacy,” said Paolo Ardoino, CEO of Tether. “Collaboration with international technology leaders unlocks new opportunities for developing the digital infrastructure of Kazakhstan’s financial sector. results.title: In the Wake of CLARITY Act's Failure, Agencies Move
highlights: For years, the crypto industry has pushed for clarity on U.S. law and a regulatory framework to legitimize the U.S. market and encourage institutional adoption. Industry hopes for clarity were high last summer. On July 17, 2025, Congress passed the GENIUS Act and the House passed the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R. 3633) [1] (CLARITY) by a 294-134 vote. On September 15, 2026, after more than a year of bipartisan Senate committee work and a last-minute release of revised substitute text, [2] the Senate rejected cloture on the motion to proceed on the bill by a vote of 49-50 (with one senator not voting), 11 votes short of the 60 needed to open floor debate. With the Senate approaching its recess ahead of the November 2026 midterms, the bill is effectively dead for the remainder of this Congress. But who needs CLARITY anyway? Federal agencies are not waiting for Congress. On August 18, 2026, weeks before the Senate’s failed cloture vote, the SEC proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, [4] which includes a two-tier fundraising exemption of up to $20 million for Tier 1 and up to $75 million for Tier 2 in a 12-month period, plus a separate $5 million/four-year startup exemption, along with a conditional safe harbor for crypto assets that meet its conditions. The proposal reflects the SEC’s view that it can use existing exemptive and interpretive authority to create a tailored pathway for qualifying offerings. [5] An agency-created exemption, however, rests on a different legal foundation than a statutory exemption or statutory directive to prescribe such rules, such as the congressional directive for the SEC to adopt Regulation Crypto included in the failed CLARITY bill. The failed cloture vote does not change the SEC’s existing statutory authority to proceed with proposed Regulation Crypto Assets. On September 24, 2026, the CFTC’s Market Participants Division, Division of Market Oversight, and Division of Clearing and Risk released updates to FAQs Concerning Registrant and Registered Entity Activities Relating to Crypto Assets and Blockchain Technologies. [11] The FAQs, [12] which were originally released on March 20, 2026, were updated to address investments of customer funds in tokenized forms of permitted investments under CFTC Regulation 1.25 and the use of blockchain (or distributed ledger) technologies to satisfy a registrant’s recordkeeping requirements. The post-CLARITY failure regulatory activity is consistent with the direction from House Financial Services Chair French Hill and House Agriculture Chair Glenn Thompson: “Until statutory certainty is achieved, we look forward to partnering with the federal financial regulators as they utilize existing authorities to develop rules and issue guidance governing digital assets.” [13] These measures can advance discrete aspects of the market-structure agenda, but they do not eliminate the need for Congress to address the core statutory gaps left in the wake of CLARITY’s failure. Without congressional action, the CFTC cannot create a registration and licensing regime for spot digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers using its existing authority alone. Under the Commodity Exchange Act, the agency’s authority in spot commodity markets is limited to anti-fraud and anti-manipulation enforcement. It has no existing statutory basis to require those spot intermediaries to register or to impose the ongoing supervisory, capital, conduct, and compliance obligations that would accompany a comprehensive federal regime. Agencies can approximate some of what CLARITY would have done, particularly on capital formation and product innovation, but core structural pieces, most importantly a durable spot-market intermediary licensing regime, bankruptcy protection for customers, and BSA classification, require an act of Congress. Industry participants continue to play a vital role in the creation of a legitimate U.S. regulatory framework. Troutman Pepper Locke is preparing responses to the agencies’ requests for comments. Industry participants interested in sharing their views relating to matters for which the agencies have requested comment should reach out before the applicable deadline. Comments for the SEC’s proposed Regulation Crypto Assets are due October 20, 2026. highlights: Morpho Blue and how it enables our vision for DeFi lending > Today, we published the whitepaper and released the code of Morpho Blue, a new lending protocol. Today, we published the whitepaper and released the code of Morpho Blue, a new lending protocol. Morpho Blue’s narrow focus enables trustless and efficient lending and borrowing of assets. It provides users with higher collateralization factors, improved interest rates, significantly reduced gas costs, and permissionless market creation. , Morpho Blue spent two years , Morpho must metamorph current state of We call this evolution Morpho Blue 🟦. What is Morpho Blue Morpho Blue is a trustless and efficient lending primitive with permissionless market creation. It enables the deployment of minimal and isolated lending markets by specifying one loan asset, one collateral asset, a liquidation LTV (LLTV), and an oracle. The protocol is trustless and was designed to be more efficient and flexible than any other decentralized lending protocol. - Immutable Morpho Blue is not upgradable. The protocol will run and behave the same way forever. - Governance-minimized Morpho Governance cannot halt the operation of a market or control funds for users’ behalf, nor does it impose specific oracle implementations. Instead, risk management is externalized to the above layers. - Simple The protocol consists of only 650 lines of Solidity code. This simplicity makes it particularly easy to understand and safe. - Higher collateralization factors Morpho Blue’s Lending markets are isolated. Unlike multi-asset pools, liquidation parameters for each market can be set without consideration of the most risky asset in the basket. Therefore, suppliers can lend at a much higher LLTV while being exposed to the same market risk as when supplying to a multi-asset pool with a lower LLTV. - Improved interest rates Collateral assets are not lent out to borrowers. This alleviates the liquidity requirements for liquidations to function properly in current lending protocols and allows Morpho Blue to offer higher capital utilization. Moreover, Morpho Blue is fully autonomous, so it does not need to introduce fees to cover costs for protocol maintenance, risk managers, or code security experts. - (Very) low gas costs Morpho Blue is a remarkably simple protocol built in a singleton smart contract that groups every possible primitive market in the same place. This reduces gas consumption by 70% compared to existing lending protocols. - Permissionless market creation Morpho Blue features permissionless asset listing. Markets with any collateral and loan assets and any risk parametrization can be created. The protocol also supports permissioned markets, enabling a broader range of use cases, including RWAs and institutional markets. - Permissionless risk management Morpho Blue is designed to serve as a simple, foundational building block that allows adding more logic layers on top. These layers can enhance the core functionality by handling risk management and compliance or simplify the user experience for passive lenders.For example, risk experts could build noncustodial curated vaults for lenders to earn yield passively. Those vaults recreate the current multi-collateral lending pools but on top of a trustless and efficient protocol. In fact, any lending pool with any asset and any risk management method can be built on this unique primitive. Morpho Blue’s code is released under a Business Source License 1.1. under the name of the nonprofit Morpho Association but controlled by the Morpho Governance, made up of MORPHO token holders. It is important to note that the license will convert to GPL after two years or if the protocol fee switch is activated. Morpho Blue is designed to serve as the foundation for DeFi lending. Onchain and offchain applications can be built on top to manage risk-return, handle compliance, enhance usability, and more. Users can interact with the primitive directly or can delegate certain tasks to different layers depending on their specific needs. We believe multiple highly specialized layers that enrich the protocol’s core functionality — similar to UniswapX for UniswapV4 — are crucial for unlocking DeFi’s true potential. In particular, we believe the risk management layer deserves its own protocol. More information will be released as we move closer to testnet deployment in the coming weeks.
